title: Study 1: Soil water content and bean germination
bodyMd:
**Research summary.** Students investigated how the amount of water held in soil affects the germination of two bean varieties, *Variety R* and *Variety S*.

**Procedure.** Forty identical trays were filled with the same sterilised potting mix. Each tray received 50 seeds of a single variety. All trays were held in one growth chamber at $22^{\circ}\text{C}$ with 16 hours of light per day. Each tray was weighed twice daily and water was added so that the tray stayed at one of four *soil water contents* — 10%, 20%, 30% or 40% of the soil mass. Five trays were used for each combination of variety and water content ($2 \times 4 \times 5 = 40$ trays).

After 10 days the students recorded, for each tray, the percent of the 50 seeds that had germinated and the mean root length of the seedlings, in millimetres. Table 1 reports the mean of the five trays in each group.

data.caption: Table 1. Mean germination percentage and mean root length after 10 days, by variety and soil water content (five trays per group, 50 seeds per tray).

accessibilityText: A research summary describing a germination experiment, followed by Table 1, which has four rows and five columns. The columns are soil water content as a percent, Variety R germination percent, Variety S germination percent, Variety R mean root length in millimetres, and Variety S mean root length in millimetres. Row one, 10 percent soil water: Variety R germinated 18 percent with mean root length 9 millimetres; Variety S germinated 42 percent with mean root length 21 millimetres. Row two, 20 percent: Variety R 56 percent and 24 millimetres; Variety S 78 percent and 38 millimetres. Row three, 30 percent: Variety R 88 percent and 41 millimetres; Variety S 74 percent and 33 millimetres. Row four, 40 percent: Variety R 62 percent and 30 millimetres; Variety S 40 percent and 16 millimetres. Variety R reaches its highest germination at 30 percent soil water, and Variety S reaches its highest at 20 percent. The accompanying line graph plots the two germination columns against soil water content and contains no information beyond the table.

provenance.notes: Original experiment description and invented data set written for this bank. The two bean varieties, the procedure and every figure in Table 1 are fictional. Nothing here is drawn from, or modelled on, any ACT-published Science passage or any real published study.
